source_text: Et dixit Deus: faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram, et principetur piscibus maris et volatilibus caeli et bestiis universae terrae. Talem hominem vult Deus principatum gerere praedictarum bestiarum. Aquae — mens — sensum spiritalem producat; terra — caro — sensum carnis; dominetur nus, non illa ei. Considera magnitudinem: cetera iussione fiunt — fiat firmamentum, congregetur aqua — at de homine: faciamus. Solum caelum et terra, luminaria, et homo factura ipsius Dei ascribuntur.
pass_a_gloss: And said God: let-us-make human to image and likeness our, and let-him-rule fishes of-sea and birds of-heaven and beasts of-whole earth. Such human wants God rule to-bear of-aforesaid beasts. Waters — mind — sense spiritual let-produce; earth — flesh — sense of-flesh; let-rule mind, not those to-him. Consider greatness: other-things by-command are-made — let-be firmament, let-be-gathered water — but about human: let-us-make. Only heaven and earth, lights, and human making of-God-himself are-ascribed.
pass_b_english: [[God said: Let us make humankind in our image and likeness, and let them rule the fish of the sea and the birds of heaven and the beasts of the whole earth >> Bible:Genesis 1:26]]. God wants such a human to hold rule over those beasts already named. Let the waters — the mind — bring forth spiritual sense; let the earth — the flesh — put forth fleshly sense; and let the mind rule, not those over it. Mark the greatness: other things are made by command — [[Let there be a firmament >> Bible:Genesis 1:6]], [[Let the water be gathered >> Bible:Genesis 1:9]] — but of the human: Let us make. Only heaven and earth, the lights, and the human are ascribed as God’s own making.
